extracted.intended_audience: BBC editorial staff, programme makers, journalists and BBC content producers
extracted.subtask_description: High-level editorial standards and guidance for producing BBC TV, radio and online content, covering values (accuracy, impartiality, privacy), procedural requirements (mandatory referrals, re-use), and audience-interaction rules (phone-ins, competitions, social media). This page is an index/entry point to the BBC's Editorial Guidelines and supplementary guidance notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Editorial Guidelines (BBC's values and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editorial Guidelines are the BBC's values and standards. They apply to all our content, wherever and however it is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching standard: all BBC output must comply with these values and standards. The page acts as an index to more detailed sections and guidance notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes (supplementary guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes supplement the Editorial Guidelines, with further explanation of their themes and practical tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these guidance notes for practical advice and expanded explanation of the main principles when producing or commissioning content.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Air References to Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for using hashtags and calls to action which involve using Twitter & Facebook and other social media platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance is designed to help programme makers share views and comments on the right occasions and in the right way; it governs when and how to refer to social media, use hashtags, and invite audience action.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Style Guide (clarity and script-writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-written story is the easiest to understand so have a look at the News Style Guide on the BBC Co-Jo. It's invaluable for avoiding common script-writing pitfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the News Style Guide to ensure clear, well-structured copy for broadcast and online news; it addresses style, phrasing, and common scripting errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is a core theme of the Editorial Guidelines and is covered by training modules and a dedicated section (Section 3: Accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should follow the Accuracy section when finding and checking contributors and information; training modules are available on accuracy and mandatory referral rules may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality is a central editorial value (including the BBC Trust Impartiality Report which examines areas such as immigration, the EU and religion and ethics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output must be impartial; editorial teams should consult impartiality guidance and reports to understand topical sensitivities and ensure balanced coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness, Contributors and Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance covering fairness to contributors, access agreements, consent and related mandatory referrals (Section 6 and related pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules on contributor treatment, consent processes, access agreements, and when referrals or additional safeguards are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymity appears as a specific topic within the Fairness/Contributors and Consent guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out when and how contributors may be anonymised and the editorial considerations and protections necessary when granting anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Privacy principles and mandatory referral rules are set out (Section 7: Privacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers expectations around private information, legal and ethical privacy considerations, and when to refer issues for higher-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret Recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Secret Recording is addressed as a specific risk/privacy topic within the guidelines (Section 7 and training modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when secret recording may be permissible, the legal and ethical constraints, and the editorial tests to apply before broadcasting such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children and Young People as Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance on interacting with children and young people, including consent, risk, privacy and safeguarding (Section 9 and related guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Part 1 (Online Child Safety), Part 2 (Risk, Privacy and Consent), working-with-children procedures and mandatory referrals for sensitive cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm and Offence (including Imitative Behaviour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on harm and offence covers subjects such as imitative behaviour and other harms that content might cause (Section 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets editorial boundaries and risk assessments to avoid encouraging imitation of dangerous acts or causing undue offence; training modules cover related topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Relationships and Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and principles governing relationships with external organisations and funding (Section 16, Parts A–C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details what funding must conform to the Statement of Policy on Alternative Finance, mandatory referrals, principles for co-productions, and how to handle external relationships to preserve editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising, Sponsorship and the BBC Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising and Sponsorship Guidelines for BBC Commercial Services and rules on advertising and the BBC brand are referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets boundaries between editorial content and commercial interests; includes specific guidance for BBC commercial services and on maintaining the integrity of the BBC brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-Use and Reversioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on re-using factual programmes and reversioning content (Section 13: Re-Use and Reversioning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes principles and mandatory referral points to ensure rights, permissions, editorial suitability and attribution are correctly handled when re-using material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interacting with our Audiences (phone-ins, UGC, competitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive guidance covering phone-in programmes, user-generated content online, mobile content, games, interactive TV, and other audience interactions (Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers rules and principles for telephone services, prizes, pre-recorded/repeated programmes, awards, voting, competitions, talent shows and life-changing opportunities, plus mandatory referrals and the role of ITACU (Interactivity Technical Advice and Contracts Unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitions, Voting and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific code of conduct and mandatory referral rules for competitions, voting and phone-ins (Appendix 2 and Section 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets fairness, transparency and legal/consumer-protection requirements for running competitions and votes, and when issues must be escalated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles to safeguard editorial integrity and independence from external interests (Section 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance to ensure editorial decisions are not improperly influenced by sponsors, funders or other external parties; includes referral and disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles, Responsibilities and Using the Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on roles and responsibilities, principles and practices, editorial justification and how to use the Guidelines (Section 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains who is responsible for decisions, when guidance must be followed, the need for editorial justification for unusual decisions, and where to find further advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that departs from normal practice or raises significant issues must have clear editorial justification (referenced under 'Editorial Justification' in Section 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires producers to document the reasons for editorial choices that might otherwise be questioned and to seek mandatory referrals when thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Compliance (BBC Academy modules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training modules are available via the BBC Academy covering topics such as Accuracy, Impartiality, Strong Language, Violence, Secret Recording, Consent, Children and other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and staff are expected to undertake relevant training modules to understand and apply the guidelines in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and the BBC Charter
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountability principles and the BBC Charter and Agreement are referenced as foundational governance frameworks (Section 19 and Section 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial practice must be consistent with the BBC Charter and Agreement; accountability mechanisms and reports (e.g., BBC Trust reports) inform editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Sources and External Regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and references to related sources of advice and regulation such as Ofcom Broadcasting Code, BBC Complaints, Defence Advisory Notice Committee and other external sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial teams must consult external regulator codes and complaints processes where relevant and understand when external guidance supersedes or complements BBC internal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on finding contributors is referenced under Section 3 and other related pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for sourcing contributors, checking credibility and consent, and applying relevant sections (privacy, anonymity, fairness) when engaging contributors.
